To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a novel crowd-sourced framework is developed to enable persistent-monitoring of the ocean by multiple users; 2) this framework enables the crowd to retask a marine robot in real-time to achieve science objectives; 3) this framework enables users to view current vehicle state and science data, as well as predict future vehicle state and ocean features; and 4) this framework is demonstrated to be effective in maximizing the sum of observed values of nitrate.
crowds can be used as an effective tool for the retasking of persistent monitoring vehicles to achieve desired science objectives.
we have developed a framework that enables a crowd-sourced decision making system to retask a Wave Glider in real-time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a system that enables crowds to control marine robots in order to optimize the science objectives of the missions.
the development and implementation of a persistent monitoring framework that utilizes crowdsourcing to enable the control of autonomous marine robots over long periods of operation.
enabling the crowd-sourced control of marine robots, and the associated decision-support system, to enable the persistent monitoring of the ocean.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our system enables the control of an autonomous marine robot by anyone with an internet-enabled computer, tablet, or smartphone.

our framework provides the ability to crowd-source the control of a vehicle in a persistent monitoring mission, enabling the control of the vehicle by a team of scientists working in a shift-based fashion, and the ability to adapt the vehicle's behavior to the ocean's dynamics.
our framework is an effective means to enable persistent monitoring of marine environments through crowd-sourcing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully demonstrated the ability to crowd-source the control of a persistent monitoring vehicle.
the use of crowdsourcing for persistent monitoring of the ocean through a decision support system is feasible.

we have successfully demonstrated the feasibility of using a crowdsourcing platform to enable a team of scientists to control a Wave Glider to collect data over an extended period of time, and that the crowd-sourced data collected was comparable to the data collected by an autonomous algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
crowd-sourcing can be a viable option for persistent monitoring of the ocean.

crowds can be used to extend the autonomy and science objectives of a persistent-monitoring vehicle, and that the crowd-sourcing approach can be used to provide a more efficient and effective solution than traditional approaches.
crowds are capable of making decisions that can be used to control autonomous vehicles for persistent monitoring.
